body:
When a vape stops producing vapor, or the puffs turn weak, thin or cool, it is rarely a mystery for long. The cause is usually one of a short list: a flat battery, no liquid, blocked airflow, a loose connection, a flooded or worn coil, extreme temperature or a locked device. This guide walks through the checks in the order that finds the problem fastest, explains what each symptom means, shows how to fix the cause for each type of device, covers disposables, pods and tanks separately, lists what not to do and explains when a device has simply reached the end of its life. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive.

## Start with what the device is telling you
Before you take anything apart, notice how it behaves. Does it fire at all? Does a light blink, and in what pattern? Is the vapor weak, or absent, or harsh? Does the problem happen on every puff or only some? Those clues narrow the field. A device that does nothing and shows no light points to power. A device that fires but gives no vapor points to liquid or airflow. A device that gives thin vapor and a flat taste points to a worn coil or low power. Keep those clues in mind as you go through the checks.

## 1. Battery
A flat battery is the most common cause. Charge a rechargeable device for 20 to 30 minutes, then try again. A device with a nearly empty battery may fire weakly before it stops, so a gradual fade is a sign of low charge. Many devices have a light that blinks when the battery is low. See [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) and [understanding vape device indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/). If the device will not charge, see [what to do when a vape will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/).

## 2. Out of liquid
Check the window or the pod. A dry wick burns and gives weak or harsh vapor, and a device that is out of liquid may still fire and heat the coil. Refill a refillable pod or tank, or replace a pre-filled pod. In a disposable, if you cannot see liquid and the flavor has gone, the device may be finished. Do not keep puffing on an empty device, because it burns the wick and gives an unpleasant taste.

## 3. Blocked airflow
Airflow holes can be covered by fingers or lint, and in some devices the sensor channel can be blocked by condensation. Check that your fingers are not over the intake, and clean the holes gently with a dry cotton bud. If the draw feels very tight, airflow may be blocked. If you have an adjustable airflow ring, check that it is not fully closed. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## 4. Loose connection
Make sure the pod or tank is seated firmly, with a click if it has one, and that the contacts are clean. Wipe the metal contacts with a dry cotton bud. Liquid residue or lint can stop the electrical connection, so the device will not fire. If a pod has a bent or dirty contact, clean it carefully, and do not bend anything.

## 5. Flooded coil
Too much liquid can drown the coil, so that it cannot heat the liquid properly. Signs are gurgling, weak vapor and sometimes leaking. Blow gently through the mouthpiece, wipe excess liquid from the contacts and wait a few minutes. See [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/) and [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

## 6. Worn coil
Coils lose performance with time, as residue builds up on the heating surface. Flavor fades, vapor thins and sometimes a burnt taste appears. Replace the coil or pod. As a rough guide, coils last from several days to a few weeks depending on use, liquid and power. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## 7. Cold or hot temperatures
Batteries struggle in cold, and a device left in a cold car or outdoors may fire weakly or not at all. Warm the device in your hand or an inside pocket, away from heat sources, and let it reach room temperature. Very hot conditions are also a problem: a device that has been in the sun can shut off to protect itself. Let it cool before you try again. Never use a hairdryer or a heater to warm a battery.

## 8. Device lock
Some devices lock after multiple clicks, to prevent accidental firing in a pocket. Check the manual for the unlock sequence, which is often a set number of clicks on the button. If your device has a lock indicator, it may blink in a particular pattern.

## 9. The sensor is stuck
In auto-draw devices, a small sensor detects your inhale. Condensation can make it stick. Blowing gently into the mouthpiece, or tapping the device against your palm, can free it. Wipe away any visible liquid, and let it sit upright for a few minutes.

## 10. Prime the coil
A new coil or pod that has not been primed can seem to give nothing, or taste burnt. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/). Let it soak, and use gentle puffs at first.

## Troubleshooting by device type
### Disposables
You cannot open or repair a disposable. Check the charge, check for liquid, clear the mouthpiece and the airflow, and try holding it upright for a minute. If it still does not work, it may be faulty or finished.

### Pod systems
Remove the pod and check the contacts and the liquid. Try a fresh pod, if you have one, to tell whether the problem is the pod or the battery. Clean the contacts, and make sure the pod clicks fully into place.

### Tank and mod systems
Check the battery level, the connection between tank and mod, the coil and the power setting. Try a different coil, or put the tank on another mod, to isolate the fault. Make sure the coil's resistance is displayed correctly. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## What not to do
- **Do not open a disposable or a sealed device.** It risks damaging the battery.
- **Do not use metal tools in the charging port or contacts.**
- **Do not keep vaping on a dry or burnt coil.** It tastes bad and wears the coil.
- **Do not heat a battery to warm it up.**
- **Do not force a pod that does not fit.** Check it is the right model.

## A quick diagnostic flow
If nothing happens at all, check the charge and the lock. If it fires but there is no vapor, check the liquid and the airflow. If vapor is thin and flavor is flat, check the coil and the power. If it gurgles, check for flooding. If it tastes burnt, check the liquid level and the coil. Following that order solves most cases within a few minutes.

## When the device has reached its end
Batteries wear and coils wear. A device that has been in use for a long time may simply be finished. If a disposable has run out of liquid or battery, replace it, and dispose of it properly. See [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). If a refillable device has a worn battery, consider a replacement.

## If your device is faulty from new
If a device from us does not work, or stops working very soon, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order ID and a description of what you tried. Our [refund policy](/refunds/) explains what applies, and we will tell you the next step. Do not try to repair it.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does my vape work for one puff and then stop?
Often a flooded coil, a low battery or a sensor that is sticking. Wipe, wait and try again.

### Why is the vapor weak even though the battery is full?
A worn coil, low liquid, blocked airflow or too low a power setting.

### Why does my device blink but not fire?
Blinking is a signal. Check the manual or our guide to indicator lights. It can mean low battery, a short circuit or a lock.

### Can a cold device be fixed by warming it?
Usually yes, by letting it return to room temperature. Do not use direct heat.

### Is it normal for a vape to need replacing?
Yes. Coils and batteries are consumables, and devices have a limited life.

## Prevention
Charge before it is empty, keep liquid above the minimum, prime new coils, avoid chain vaping and store devices upright at room temperature. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) when you need replacements. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Three short case studies
### Case 1: the pocket device
A customer's pod device worked in the morning and stopped by lunchtime. The battery light blinked three times. The cause was a low battery, and a 25-minute charge fixed it. Lesson: a blinking light on a device that suddenly stops is usually a power signal.

### Case 2: the weak vapor
A tank gave thin, cool vapor even with a full battery. The coil had been in use for three weeks, and the cotton looked dark and crusty. A new coil, primed properly, restored full flavor. Lesson: weak vapor with a full battery points to the coil.

### Case 3: the cold morning
A disposable did nothing when taken out of a cold car. After ten minutes in an inside pocket, it worked normally. Lesson: warm the device gently and give it time.

## A small troubleshooting kit
Keep a few simple items to hand: a spare cable, a dry cotton bud, a wooden toothpick, paper towels and a spare pod or coil. With these, you can solve most problems in a few minutes without leaving the house.

faq.a: Flavor fades, vapor thins and sometimes a burnt taste appears. Replace the coil or pod.
